the LDE in Tunisia is characterized by a short-term warming, but that the associated CIE is missing, possibly because of condensation or a hiatus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LDE was a regional event, which was not recorded in the shallowest sections in Tunisia, and which is not associated with a major benthic forminiferal assemblage change.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to Egypt, the Danian sections in Tunisia do not contain a condensed sequence at the base of subzone P3b, and that the LDE in Tunisia is not recorded by a CIE in the benthic forams.
the LDE is not a global event in the sense that it is not recorded in all sections.

the Tunisian and Egyptian sequences are similar in terms of paleobathymetry and paleoenvironment, which makes the Tunisian sections an ideal reference section for the Danian in the Mediterranean region and for correlation with sections in the Nile Basin.
